chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who set out performing tamattuʿ with ʿumrah toward hajj, but did not reach Makkah until the Day of Sacrifice, so he said:

He remains in Makkah in his state of ihram, stops the talbiyah when he enters the Haram, then performs tawaf of the House, performs saʿy, shaves his head, slaughters his sheep, and then returns to his family.

Then he said: This is for the one who made a condition with his Lord at the time of his ihram that He would release him wherever he was prevented. But if he did not make such a condition, then hajj and ʿumrah are upon him in the following year.

key_terms.إِحْرَامِهِ: his state of ritual consecration for pilgrimage rites
key_terms.عُمْرَةٍ: the lesser pilgrimage performed before hajj in tamattuʿ
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعاً: one performing tamattuʿ, combining ʿumrah with hajj in a specific form
key_terms.ٱلتَّلْبِيَةَ: the pilgrimage invocation recited in ihram
key_terms.ٱلنَّحْرِ: the Day of Sacrifice, when ritual slaughter is performed during hajj
key_terms.ٱلْعُمْرَةَ: the lesser pilgrimage obligation mentioned here for the following year

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone performing tamattuʿ who reaches Makkah only on the Day of Sacrifice?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person intending tamattuʿ who reaches Makkah only on Yawm al-Nahr. It explains what he should do if he had stipulated a condition at the time of ihram, and states that if he had not made that condition, he must perform both hajj and ʿumrah in the following year.
